model: Clients i=1..n with integer turnover times tau_i; a schedule serves S_t on day t and must serve client i at least once in every tau_i consecutive days. Daily cost f(S_t) with f normalised, monotone, submodular (rooted-tree routing: f_T(S)=sum_e 2c_e [S meets D(e)]). Objective: long-run average cost; OPT is the infimum over all feasible repeating schedules (individual gaps may vary). Frequency bound L_f = sum a_i/tau_i with greedy weights a_i.

claims.statement: A deterministic O(n log n) algorithm with n+1 oracle calls returns a feasible integer calendar with cycle P <= tau_max and average cost <= W_1 + (L_f - W_1)/ln 2 <= OPT/ln 2. On rooted trees this improves the factor 2 of Bosman et al. (2022) against the same optimum.

sup OPT_short/OPT = 1/ln 2, where OPT_short is restricted to schedules repeating within tau_max days; the witness stars with turnovers M..2M-1 (plus an epsilon trunk) show the analysis of the full algorithm is tight on trees.

Constant-gap calendars from divisor chains: mixtures give deterministic constant-gap algorithms with factors 12/7, 48/29 and <= 1.60139 (17 chains). Every calendar with integer pairwise-dividing constant gaps costs >= 1.60010 OPT on an explicit 17-leaf star. Hence 1.60010 <= rho_H <= 1.60139.
claims.evidence: written proof plus exact rational certificate (verify_constant_gap_chains.py, data/constant_gap_chain_certificates.json)

claims.statement: Exact optimum of two nested edges with maximum gaps a<=b, costs u,v: u/a+v/b + min{(a-r)u/(ab), r v/(m a b)} with b=ma+r.
claims.evidence: written proof; numerical and exact cross-checks

claims.statement: The frequency bound is attained on a tree iff q_e divides q_g for every positive-cost ancestor-descendant edge pair; for weighted coverage costs iff lcm{q_A : i in A} <= tau_i for every client.
claims.evidence: written proofs; 192 tree and 100 coverage exact certificates

claims.statement: OPT_T >= L_T + Z for the pooled pairwise LP value Z.
Every single harmonic ladder costs >= 1 on the witness stars (ratio -> 1/ln 2); the cycle-budget profile g(h) satisfies g(B/M) <= min_{P<=B} C_M(P) <= g(B/M)+1/M.
